styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Ceviche, causa and long lunches in Miraflores and Barranco.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Colonial plazas, catacombs and pre-Inca ruins in the centre.

styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Museums, street art and Barranco's bohemian nights.

stays.why: Safe, walkable and central for visitors. Parks, cafés and the cliff-top malecón are close; most tours pick up here.
Bohemian streets, galleries and nightlife. Good for food and music; quieter and cheaper than Miraflores.
Business district with leafy streets and upscale hotels. Calm at night; a short taxi to Miraflores and the centre.
Closest to the Plaza de Armas, cathedral and museums. Busy and less polished at night; check your street.

food: Try ceviche at lunch, not dinner: it is a midday dish. A set lunch (menú del día) costs about S/15–30.
Book a top restaurant like Central or Maido weeks ahead; cheaper spots in Barranco are walk-in friendly.
Criollo classics: lomo saltado, ají de gallina and anticuchos (grilled skewers) from street stalls in the evening.
Coffee and sweets: try a picarón (fried dough with syrup) and local coffee in Miraflores.
Tap water is not for drinking; buy bottled water. Be careful with raw street food if your stomach is sensitive.
more_time: Add a day for Pachacámac ruins and the beach suburb of Punta Hermosa south of the city.
Swap one city day for a boat trip to the Ballestas Islands and Paracas, about 3 hours south by bus.
Food lovers can add a cooking class or a market tour at Surquillo or Mercado de Magdalena.

recommend.why: Three nights covers the historic centre, Miraflores and Barranco with time for a serious meal; add a night for a day trip south.

month_notes: January: warm and mostly dry, highs near 25°C. Good beach weather south of the city.
February: the warmest month, highs near 26°C. A few rain days; pack a light layer for evenings.
March: still warm, highs near 25°C, with the most rain days of the year (about 7).
April: warm and drier, highs near 24°C. Comfortable for walking the centre.
May: cooler and grey, highs near 22°C. The coastal fog (garúa) starts; bring a jacket.
June: grey and cool, highs near 20°C, no rain. Damp mornings; layers help.
July: the coolest, greyest month, highs near 19°C. No rain but little sun.
August: cool and grey, highs near 19°C. Same as July; plan indoor sights and long lunches.
September: still cool and grey, highs near 19°C. Fog eases slowly.
October: mild, highs near 20°C, one rain day. A good shoulder month.
November: brighter and warmer, highs near 21°C. Pleasant for sightseeing.
December: warm and mostly dry, highs near 23°C. Busy holiday season; book ahead.

climate_guide.summary: Mild desert coast: warm and sunny December to April, cool and grey May to November. Rain is rare; the fog is the main weather story.

items.title: Best time: December to April
items.text: Warm days around 23–26°C and little rain. Best for the beach and long walks.

items.title: Grey season (May to November)
items.text: Cool, damp fog called garúa. Highs drop to about 19–22°C and the sun is rare. Pack a jacket.

items.title: Very little rain
items.text: Most months see zero rain days. March is the wettest with about 7 days, still light.

items.title: Cold sea
items.text: The Pacific here is chilly most of the year. Swimming is for the brave; beaches south are warmer in summer.

items.title: Layers, not umbrellas
items.text: Mornings are damp and cool even in summer. A light jacket and comfortable shoes work all year.

items.title: Sun in summer
items.text: December to April the sun is strong. Use sunscreen and a hat on the malecón and at ruins.

transit.best: Ride apps or agreed-price taxis for most trips; walk in Miraflores and Barranco.

modes.text: Line 1 is elevated and runs north-south east of the centre. It misses most tourist areas, so it is rarely useful for visitors.
Metropolitano is a fast bus rapid transit with dedicated lanes. Card costs S/4.5 and the fare is S/2.50. City buses and combis are cheap but confusing; agree the fare first.
Uber, DiDi and Cabify work in Lima; check the driver name and plate before getting in. Street taxis have no meters: agree the price first and confirm soles, not dollars.
Driving is chaotic. Only rent if you plan to leave the city; parking and traffic are hard.
Fine in Miraflores and Barranco, and bike lanes are growing. Use care in the historic centre at night.
